## Problem

## Requirements

- Input: an $$m \times n$$ grid named `grid`; its values may be below zero. The function signature is `max_path_sum(grid: list[list[int]]) -> int`.
- Moves are limited to the four orthogonal neighbors: up, down, left, and right.
- Goal: choose a cell path that never uses the same cell twice and has the largest possible total of its cell values. The path may start and end at any cells.

## Notes

- Do not mistake this for the standard matrix dynamic-programming exercise that travels from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner using only right and down moves. That restricted version is polynomial; verify both the allowed moves and the no-revisit rule before coding.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of this as a longest-path problem in a grid graph, which is NP-hard in general, but the small grid size might allow a brute-force search with pruning.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use depth-first search with memoization on the current cell and a visited set, but note that the visited set makes memoization tricky—consider using bitmask for small grids.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The trickiest part is handling negative values—you cannot stop early because a negative cell might be necessary to reach a high-value area later.

</details>
